nodes.description: Pathogenic missense variants in TMEM147 (p.Gly7Arg in transmembrane domain 1, p.Ile133Asn at the alpha-helix 5 loop facing nicalin, and p.Arg166Trp at alpha-helix 6) properly target to the endoplasmic reticulum but introduce steric clashes with TMCO1, nicalin, or adjacent TMEM147 helices. As shown in transfected COS-1 cells, these substitutions severely reduce TMEM147 protein stability and trigger accelerated protein clearance through the autophagy-lysosomal pathway, which is rescued by bafilomycin treatment.

nodes.description: At the endoplasmic reticulum membrane, TMEM147 is the core seven-transmembrane subunit of the nicalin-TMEM147-NOMO accessory complex, which assembles with the Sec61 protein-conducting channel, the Oxa1-family membrane insertase TMCO1, and CCDC47 at the ribosome exit tunnel to form a ~360 kDa translocon required for co-translational biogenesis of multi-pass membrane proteins. Depletion or steric destabilization of TMEM147 is predicted to perturb assembly and function of this multi-pass ER translocon accessory module.

nodes.description: Because LBR anchoring at the inner nuclear membrane is required for normal nuclear lobulation and heterochromatin condensation during granulocyte maturation, biallelic TMEM147 loss of function produces lobulation defects in approximately 15%–25% of peripheral blood polymorphonuclear neutrophils (and sparse eosinophils). Affected neutrophils exhibit hyposegmented or bilobed sack-like nuclei connected by a thin chromatin thread, chromatin clumping, and nuclear appendices (caryoschizes or drumsticks). Because the majority of mature granulocytes are not bilobed, this hematological finding is classified as pseudo-Pelger-Huët anomaly rather than classic Pelger-Huët anomaly.

evidence.reference_title: Bi-allelic loss-of-function variants in TMEM147 cause moderate to profound intellectual disability with facial dysmorphism and pseudo-Pelger-Huët anomaly.
evidence.snippet: Cytological examination of the blood smear frequently revealed lobulation defects of the neutrophils (Figures 5D and S3A), with forms of hyposegmentation similar to the Pelger-Huët anomaly, although with a lower proportion, bilobed aspects in the shape of a sack with two round or oval lobes connected by a thread of chromatin, rare chromatin clumping, and frequent nuclear appendices (caryoschizes or drumsticks), isolated or associated with the preceding abnormalities. These cytological abnormalities concerned about 15%–25% of neutrophils and were also identified in sparse eosinophils, indicating that the anomaly affects all granulocytes but is most evident in polymorphonuclear neutrophils (Figure S3B).

nodes.description: TMEM147 is widely expressed in the developing human brain and shows strong brain-specific co-expression with established neurodevelopmental and encephalopathy genes (including CDKL5, CLTC, KMT2E, NRXN1, SCN1A, SCN2A, TCF4, UNC80, and WDR45). Combined ER translocon impairment, RTN4/CKAP4 dysregulation, potential perturbation of nicalin-NOMO-modulated Nodal neuroectodermal patterning, and nuclear envelope dysfunction disrupt central nervous system development, manifesting as a primary developmental encephalopathy with thin corpus callosum, ventriculomegaly, delayed posterior white matter myelination, and mild cerebellar atrophy.

nodes.description: At the nuclear envelope, TMEM147 physically interacts with the C-terminal domain of lamin B receptor (LBR) to anchor LBR at the inner nuclear membrane. As demonstrated in cultured primary fibroblasts from individuals with biallelic TMEM147 variants, loss of TMEM147 abolishes this nuclear envelope restriction and causes LBR to become evenly redistributed throughout the nucleoplasm without a reduction in total LBR protein levels.

nodes.description: Biallelic truncating nonsense, frameshift, and canonical or near-canonical splice-site variants in TMEM147 (such as c.344+5G>A, which causes exon 4 skipping, and c.345-1G>T) alter the reading frame and trigger nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (except for late C-terminal frameshifts such as p.Val182Leufs*66 that replace the 6th and 7th transmembrane helices). Together with destabilizing missense variants that undergo accelerated degradation, these alleles abolish functional TMEM147 protein interactions at both the endoplasmic reticulum membrane and the inner nuclear membrane.
